key_insight: The paper explores whether coding agents can automatically build generalized task-and-motion planning solutions, reducing the need for hand-crafted TAMP engineering. The core idea is to leverage coding agents to synthesize reusable planning logic across problem instances.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of generalized task and motion planning, where discrete task choices must be coordinated with geometric, kinematic, and dynamic constraints. Existing approaches often require significant TAMP-specific manual engineering to adapt to new instances.
method: Investigate coding agents as automated designers of generalized TAMP solvers.
Use agent-generated code to capture reusable planning regularities across multiple problem instances.
Evaluate whether synthesized solutions can reduce manual effort while preserving planning effectiveness.
impact: If successful, this approach could make advanced planning systems faster to develop and easier to adapt to new robotic tasks. For practitioners, it suggests a path toward more scalable TAMP workflows with less domain-specific coding.

paper_title: Coding Agents for Generalized Task and Motion Planning Problems
paper_authors: Matteo Merler, Bowen Li, Josh Roy, Yichao Liang, Qianwei Wang
